name: Gallzein
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village on the sunny side of the Unterinntal, offering stunning views of the Zillertaler Alpen.
beschreibung:
Overview

Gallzein is situated in the Tyrolean Lower Inn Valley in the district of Schwaz, perched on a scenic mountain terrace south of the Inn River at the foot of the prominent Kellerjoch. Elevated between the historic towns of Schwaz and Jenbach, this idyllic alpine municipality covers an area of nearly eleven square kilometres. Around 705 inhabitants live scattered across picturesque hamlets including Hof, Niederleiten, Kogelmoos, Wahrbühel, Gattern, Schöllerberg, and Gasteig. Gallzein is part of the Karwendel Silver Region and represents an authentic insider tip for travellers seeking pristine nature, mountain quiet, and genuine Tyrolean farming heritage away from mass tourism. From the sunny plateau at roughly 825 metres elevation, visitors enjoy sweeping views across the Inn Valley toward the limestone crags of the Karwendel and Rofan ranges.

History

Traces of medieval settlement on this sunny slope date back to the 12th century; the settlement was first officially mentioned around 1170 as Galzins in records of the Counts of Andechs and the monastery of Herrenchiemsee. During the 15th and 16th centuries, Gallzein became closely connected to the world-famous Schwaz silver and copper mining district, with local extraction focusing particularly on high-grade iron ore for tools and regional smelters. The municipal coat of arms commemorates this heritage, depicting crossed mining hammers alongside a silver bull head representing cattle farming. The community centre lies in the hamlet of Hof, dominated by the Church of the Visitation of Mary with its distinctive wooden shingle roof. A cultural treasure of the municipality is the high density of heritage roadside and farmstead chapels. Nearby at the entrance to the Zillertal stands the imposing 12th-century fortress ruin of Kropfsberg, once guarding regional trade routes.

Getting There

By car, visitors travel via the Inntal Autobahn A12 to either the Schwaz or Wiesing/Zillertal exit. Following the federal road B171 to Buch in Tirol, drivers take the winding provincial road L217, which climbs smoothly to the mountain plateau of Gallzein in just a few minutes. Rail passengers benefit from frequent ÖBB Railjet and Intercity connections stopping at nearby Jenbach or Schwaz stations. From both railway stations, regional VVT buses (route 4111) run scheduled services directly up into Gallzein, serving stops across the main hamlets including Hof, Niederleiten, and Kogelmoos.

Tips

For hikers and nature enthusiasts, Gallzein serves as the peaceful gateway to the 2,344-metre Kellerjoch, one of the finest panoramic mountains in the Tux Alps. From the hamlet of Kogelmoos, a scenic trail winds past the rustic Kaunzalm to the iconic Kellerjoch Chapel perched on the crest, rewarding climbers with an unparalleled 360-degree vista of North Tyrol. A unique cultural highlight is the signposted 10 Chapels Trail, a gentle walking route linking historic farm chapels such as the Kobald and Fasser chapels. Families enjoy scenic loop walks between the hamlets and excursions to the historic ruins of Kropfsberg Castle and Rotholz Castle. In winter, the tranquil landscape transforms into an unspoiled haven for winter walking and snowshoeing far from crowded ski pistes.
metaDescription: Gallzein in the Karwendel Silver Region: Peaceful village on Kellerjoch, 10 Chapels Trail, Kropfsberg Castle ruins, and alpine views.
